title: Engineering Regulatory Body
summary: The Nepal Engineering Council Act 2055 (1998) is the whole basis of this subchapter, and the examinable content is the Council's functions, its registration categories and its composition. The single most useful distinction is between the Council as a statutory REGULATOR serving the PUBLIC and the Nepal Engineers' Association as a voluntary body serving its MEMBERS — which is why fixing fees or salaries is not a Council function, and why that option appears as a distractor.

sections.heading: The Nepal Engineering Council
sections.body:
**Establishment.** The **Nepal Engineering Council (NEC)** was established by the **Nepal Engineering Council Act, 2055 (1998)**, with the **Nepal Engineering Council Rules, 2057 (2000)**. It is an **autonomous statutory body** under the **Ministry of Education, Science and Technology**.

**Its purpose**, in a sentence: to **regulate the engineering profession in Nepal so as to protect the public**, by controlling who may practise, by recognising qualifications, and by enforcing standards of conduct.

**FUNCTIONS, DUTIES AND POWERS** — the examinable list:

| Function | Content |
|---|---|
| **REGISTRATION** | Maintain the **register** of engineers; issue **certificates of registration** in the prescribed categories |
| **EXAMINATION** | Conduct the **registration (license) examination** — the examination this syllabus serves |
| **RECOGNITION of qualifications** | Recognise engineering **degrees and institutions**, in Nepal and abroad |
| **ACCREDITATION** | Accredit engineering **programmes**; prescribe minimum standards of education |
| **REGULATION of conduct** | Frame and enforce the **code of ethics**; investigate complaints of **professional misconduct** |
| **DISCIPLINE** | **SUSPEND or CANCEL** registration for misconduct |
| **SCOPE OF PRACTICE** | Determine the work each **category** of registered engineer may undertake |
| Advice to Government | On engineering education and practice |
| Records and publication | Maintain and publish the register |

**What the Council does NOT do** — and this is the most examined point:

> **The Council does NOT fix the FEES or SALARIES payable to engineers.**

It is a **regulator of COMPETENCE and CONDUCT**, not a wage-fixing body. Remuneration is a matter for the **market**, for **employment contracts**, and — for public works — for the **government's own rate schedules and norms**. A professional **association** may publish recommended fee scales, but the Council does not.

That option appears as a distractor in almost every question on Council functions, and recognising why it is wrong is more useful than memorising the list: **fee-fixing serves the members' interest**, which is an association's business, not a regulator's.

**REGISTRATION CATEGORIES:**

| Category | Designation | For |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **General Engineer** | Holders of a recognised **bachelor's degree** in engineering |
| **B** | **Professional Engineer** | Engineers with **prescribed experience** and further qualification |
| **C** | **Foreign Engineer** | **Foreign nationals** practising in Nepal, for a specified period and project |

**Registration is a LEGAL PREREQUISITE to practising engineering in Nepal** — for **Nepali and foreign nationals alike**. The consequences follow directly:

> **Signing, designing, supervising or certifying engineering work without registration is an OFFENCE**, not merely an irregularity.

That is the practical significance of the whole system, and it is worth stating plainly: an unregistered person's drawings cannot lawfully be submitted for building permission, and an engineer whose registration is suspended cannot practise for the period of suspension.

**Registration requirements**: a **recognised degree** in engineering, passing the **registration examination** where required, payment of the prescribed fee, and an undertaking to abide by the **code of ethics**. Registration is **renewed periodically**, and renewal may be linked to continuing professional development.

**Disciplinary powers.** On a complaint of **professional misconduct**, the Council may investigate and, if satisfied, **reprimand**, **suspend** registration for a period, or **CANCEL** it. Cancellation removes the right to practise — the profession's ultimate sanction, and the reason the code of ethics is enforceable rather than merely aspirational.

**Grounds of professional misconduct** include: **false certification**, practising **beyond one's competence**, **negligence** causing loss or danger, **breach of the code of ethics**, obtaining registration by **misrepresentation**, and **conviction of an offence** involving moral turpitude.

**The registration examination** — which this syllabus serves — exists because a degree certifies **education** while registration must certify **readiness to practise**. Its purpose is to verify that a graduate has the **breadth of applied knowledge** a practising engineer needs across the discipline, not merely the depth of their final-year specialisation.

sections.heading: Composition, and the Council contrasted with the Association
sections.body:
**COMPOSITION of the Council** (Nepal Engineering Council Act, 2055):

| Member | Number |
|---|---|
| **Chairperson** — appointed by the Government from among distinguished engineers | 1 |
| **Government nominees** — from the Ministry and Government service | 7 |
| **President of the Nepal Engineers' Association**, ex officio | 1 |
| **Engineers ELECTED by the Nepal Engineers' Association** | 5 |
| **Nominees of the Council** itself | 2 |
| **Campus Chief** of the Institute of Engineering (or representative) | 1 |
| **Representative of the Institute of Engineering / engineering education** | 1 |
| **REGISTRAR — Member-Secretary** | 1 |

**The Registrar is the Member-Secretary** — the chief executive officer, responsible for the register, the day-to-day administration and the execution of the Council's decisions. That the Registrar is Member-Secretary rather than a voting member is the standard detail asked.

**Note the composition's logic:** it combines **government** representation (accountability for a statutory function), **profession** representation (through the NEA-elected members and the NEA President), and **education** representation (the Institute of Engineering) — reflecting that the Council's functions span all three domains.

**THE CENTRAL DISTINCTION — Council and Association:**

| | **Nepal Engineering Council (NEC)** | **Nepal Engineers' Association (NEA)** |
|---|---|---|
| **Nature** | **STATUTORY REGULATOR**, created by the Act | **VOLUNTARY** membership body |
| **Joining** | **REGISTRATION IS MANDATORY** to practise | **By choice** |
| **Powers** | **Licensing**; the registration examination; **SUSPEND or CANCEL** registration | Advocacy, professional development, networking, publications |
| **Whose interest it serves** | **THE PUBLIC** | **ITS MEMBERS** |
| **Fees and salaries** | **Does NOT fix them** | May publish **recommended** fee scales |
| Funding | Registration fees; statutory | Membership subscriptions |
| Sanction available | Removal of the right to practise | Expulsion from membership only |

> **A REGULATOR exists to protect the PUBLIC. An ASSOCIATION exists to advance its MEMBERS' interests.**

That single sentence resolves most questions in the subchapter, including the fee-fixing one: **fee-fixing serves members**, so it belongs to an association, not a regulator. And it explains why the Council's sanction is so much heavier — an association can only expel a member from its own body, while a regulator can remove the right to work.

**The two are nonetheless LINKED**, and the composition above shows how: the **NEA President sits ex officio** on the Council and the **NEA elects five members** to it. So the profession has a substantial voice in its own regulation — which is the ordinary arrangement for a self-regulating profession, and the reason such bodies are described as exercising **delegated self-regulation** rather than pure external regulation.

**The tension inherent in that arrangement** is worth recognising: a body largely composed of members of the profession it regulates may be tempted to serve the profession rather than the public. The safeguards are the **statutory mandate** (which states whose interest is paramount), the **government nominees**, and the **published code of ethics** against which the Council's own decisions can be judged.

**Comparable bodies elsewhere**, for context:

| Country | Body |
|---|---|
| **Nepal** | **Nepal Engineering Council (NEC)** |
| India | Institution of Engineers (India) — chartered, but **no statutory licensing**; state PWD registration for practice |
| United Kingdom | Engineering Council; **ICE** and other institutions |
| USA | State **Professional Engineer (PE)** licensure boards; **NCEES** examinations |
| Canada | Provincial engineering associations (**P.Eng.**) |

Note that **India has no equivalent statutory licensing body for engineers**, which is a genuine difference from Nepal and is sometimes asked. Nepal's arrangement is closer to the **US and Canadian** model of mandatory licensure than to the Indian one.

sections.heading: The regulatory framework of engineering practice in Nepal
sections.body:
**The Council operates within a wider framework of law and codes**, and a practising engineer must know which instrument governs which question.

**The principal instruments:**

| Instrument | Governs |
|---|---|
| **Nepal Engineering Council Act 2055 (1998)** and Rules 2057 | **Registration, licensing, ethics, discipline** |
| **Public Procurement Act 2063 (2007)** and Regulations 2064 | **Tendering, contracts, securities, variations** |
| **Building Act 2055 (1998)** | Building permission, building code enforcement |
| **Nepal National Building Code (NBC)** series | **Design and construction of buildings** |
| **NBC 105:2020** | **Seismic design of buildings in Nepal** |
| **NBC 202** | Mandatory Rules of Thumb for load-bearing masonry |
| **Nepal Road Standard 2070** | Road classification and geometric design |
| **Environment Protection Act 2076 (2019)** and Rules 2077 | **BES, IEE, EIA**; pollution control |
| **Electricity Act 2049 (1992)** and Rules 2050 | Hydropower survey and generation licenses |
| **Water Resources Act 2049 (1992)** | Water use rights and their **priority** |
| **Labour Act 2074 (2017)** | Workplace safety and conditions |
| **Land Acquisition Act 2034 (1977)** | Compulsory acquisition and compensation |
| **Solid Waste Management Act 2068 (2011)** | Waste responsibilities |
| **Local Government Operation Act 2074 (2017)** | Local authority functions under federalism |
| Arbitration Act 2055 (1999) | Dispute resolution |

**NBC 105:2020 deserves particular note** because it is both recent and consequential: it **replaced the 1994 edition**, introducing modern spectral shapes, **ductility classes**, and requirements reflecting the lessons of the **2015 Gorkha earthquake**. An engineer designing to the 1994 edition today is not practising competently, and questions set from older material give the superseded position.

**The relationship between Nepali and Indian standards** is worth stating clearly, because it causes confusion:

> Nepal has its own **NS (Nepal Standard)** series and its own **NBC** and road standards. But for **many materials and design procedures, Nepali practice ADOPTS or closely FOLLOWS the Indian Standards** — **IS 456** for concrete, **IS 800** for steel, **IS 1200** for measurement, the **IRC** codes for roads.

The codes with a **distinctly Nepali character** are those tied to **local conditions**: the **NBC** (particularly **NBC 105** seismic and **NBC 202** masonry), the **Nepal Road Standard 2070** (terrain classification, hairpin bends), and the standards governing **hydropower** and **water supply**, which reflect Himalayan hydrology and sediment.

**That division makes sense**: there is no reason to rewrite a concrete code, since concrete behaves the same everywhere — but seismic design, hill road geometry and sediment handling are genuinely local problems requiring local standards.

**The NS certification mark** is administered by the **Nepal Bureau of Standards and Metrology (NBSM)** under the **Nepal Standards (Certification Mark) Act, 2037 (1980)**. For certain products it is **mandatory**, and **cement is the leading example** — a consignment without valid NS certification should not be accepted on site.

**Federalism and its consequences.** Under the **Constitution of Nepal 2072 (2015)** and the **Local Government Operation Act 2074**, many functions have devolved to **provincial and local governments**:

| Level | Typical engineering functions |
|---|---|
| **Federal** | National highways, large hydropower, national standards, NEC |
| **Provincial** | Provincial roads, provincial-level infrastructure |
| **Local (municipality / rural municipality)** | **Building permission**, local roads, water supply, drainage, solid waste |

**Building permission is now a LOCAL government function**, which is significant in practice: a design must satisfy the **local bye-laws** as well as the national building code, and the **local engineer** approves it. It also means enforcement capacity varies greatly between municipalities — a genuine concern for building safety, and one the Council's registration requirement partly addresses by ensuring the designer is at least qualified.

**Professional practice arrangements** in Nepal:

| Arrangement | Character |
|---|---|
| **Government service** | Departments of Roads, Water Supply, Irrigation, Urban Development; provincial and local governments |
| **Public enterprises** | Nepal Electricity Authority, Nepal Water Supply Corporation |
| **Consulting firms** | Design, supervision, project management |
| **Contracting firms** | Construction |
| **Academia** | Teaching and research |
| **Independent practice** | Consulting individually; requires registration |

**Consulting firms** must be registered as companies and employ registered engineers; **contractors** are licensed in **classes (A to D)** by capacity, which determines the value of work they may tender for.

**The obligations that follow from registration**, as a closing summary — and they are the practical content of everything in this chapter:

| Obligation | Content |
|---|---|
| **Practise only within your COMPETENCE** | And obtain competent assistance where needed |
| **Comply with the CODE OF ETHICS** | The public interest paramount |
| **Maintain and update COMPETENCE** | Codes change; NBC 105 was revised in 2020 |
| **Sign only work you have done or checked** | A signature is a representation |
| **Keep RECORDS** | Calculations, decisions, correspondence |
| **Report serious misconduct** | To the Council |
| **Renew registration** | And meet any CPD requirement |

**And the reciprocal point, which is the real subject of this subchapter:** registration is not a formality to be completed once and forgotten. It is the **mechanism by which society grants an engineer the authority to make decisions the public cannot verify** — and the **same Council that grants that authority can remove it**. The privileges and the accountability arrive together, and an engineer who accepts the first while treating the second as optional has misunderstood what the register is for.

formulas.label: The governing Act
formulas.expression: Nepal Engineering Council Act, 2055 (1998), with Rules 2057 (2000)
formulas.note: An autonomous statutory body under the Ministry of Education, Science and Technology.

formulas.label: Council functions
formulas.expression: Registration · license EXAMINATION · recognition of qualifications and ACCREDITATION · regulation of CONDUCT · discipline (suspend or CANCEL) · scope of practice
formulas.note: It does NOT fix fees or salaries — that serves members' interests, which is an association's business.

formulas.label: Registration categories
formulas.expression: A — General Engineer ; B — Professional Engineer ; C — Foreign Engineer
formulas.note: Registration is a LEGAL PREREQUISITE to practise, for Nepali and foreign nationals alike.

formulas.label: Council composition
formulas.expression: Chairperson · 7 government nominees · NEA President ex officio · 5 NEA-elected engineers · 2 Council nominees · Campus Chief IOE · IOE representative · REGISTRAR as Member-Secretary
formulas.note: The Registrar is Member-Secretary — the chief executive, not a voting member.

formulas.label: Council versus Association
formulas.expression: NEC = STATUTORY regulator, mandatory, serves THE PUBLIC, can cancel registration. NEA = VOLUNTARY association, serves ITS MEMBERS.
formulas.note: The single distinction that resolves most questions in the subchapter.

formulas.label: Grounds of professional misconduct
formulas.expression: False certification · practising beyond competence · negligence · breach of the code · misrepresentation in obtaining registration
formulas.note: Sanctions: reprimand, suspension, or CANCELLATION of registration.

formulas.label: Nepali codes with local character
formulas.expression: NBC 105:2020 (seismic, replacing 1994) · NBC 202 (masonry rules of thumb) · Nepal Road Standard 2070 · NS certification mark
formulas.note: For concrete, steel and measurement, Nepal follows IS 456, IS 800 and IS 1200.

formulas.label: Federal division of engineering functions
formulas.expression: Federal: highways, large hydropower, standards. Provincial: provincial roads. LOCAL: BUILDING PERMISSION, local roads, water supply, drainage, waste.
formulas.note: Building permission is now a local government function under the Local Government Operation Act 2074.
